try_updating_one_row_precisely_sketch0.title: Activate the Trial Tote
try_updating_one_row_precisely_sketch0.prompt: The Trial Tote, item `6`, passed review. Change only that item's status to `active` with a scoped `UPDATE`. In `query.sql`, show items 5 and 6 in id order so the target and a nearby row can be compared. To test it in the workspace, run `operations.sql` before `query.sql`; the query file only reads the resulting database state.
try_updating_one_row_precisely_sketch0.hint: Use the item's id as the mutation boundary.

help.concept: A unique id is a strong boundary for a one-row correction.
help.hint_2: Keep a nearby row visible in verification.

single-choice-1.title: Understanding UPDATE Syntax
single-choice-1.prompt: Which SQL statement correctly updates the price of an item with id 5 to 20.00?
single-choice-1.hint: Focus on the correct use of UPDATE and WHERE clauses.

help.concept: The UPDATE statement modifies existing records in a table. Use WHERE to specify which records to update.
help.hint_1: Ensure the WHERE clause targets the correct id.
help.hint_2: The SET clause should specify the column and new value.

options.a: UPDATE inventory_items SET price = 20.00 WHERE id = 5;
options.b: UPDATE inventory_items WHERE id = 5 SET price = 20.00;
options.c: SET price = 20.00 WHERE id = 5 IN inventory_items;
options.d: UPDATE price = 20.00 FROM inventory_items WHERE id = 5;

single-choice-2.title: Purpose of WHERE Clause
single-choice-2.prompt: What is the purpose of the WHERE clause in an UPDATE statement?
single-choice-2.hint: Consider how WHERE affects which rows are updated.

help.concept: The WHERE clause specifies which rows should be updated.
help.hint_1: Without WHERE, all rows would be updated.
help.hint_2: WHERE targets specific rows based on a condition.

options.a: To specify which rows to update
options.b: To specify which columns to update
options.c: To specify the new values for columns
options.d: To specify the table to update

practice-precise-single-row-update.prompt: The Sample Poster, item `4`, was reclassified as `Art`. Use a scoped `UPDATE` so only that item receives the new category. In `query.sql`, show items 3 through 5 in id order to verify the correction beside unchanged rows. To test it in the workspace, run `operations.sql` before `query.sql`; the query file only reads the resulting database state.
practice-precise-single-row-update.hint: Use the stable item id rather than a broad text match.

help.concept: A one-row correction should use a predicate that identifies exactly that record.

sketch-1.title: Use a stable identifier for one-row corrections
sketch-1.bodyMarkdown:
When an audit approves a correction for exactly one record, a unique identifier gives the mutation a precise boundary.

```sql
UPDATE inventory_items
SET price = 50.00
WHERE id = 3;
```

The assignment defines the change; the identifier prevents the same change from spreading to unrelated rows.

sketch-2.title: Nearby rows can strengthen verification
sketch-2.bodyMarkdown:
A useful verification can show the corrected row together with nearby records.

```sql
SELECT id, name, price
FROM inventory_items
WHERE id IN (1, 2, 3)
ORDER BY id;
```

This makes it easier to confirm both sides of the result: the target changed and neighboring rows remained intact.
